action_criteria.expected_evidence: Simple fasciculation potentials without fibrillations, positive sharp waves or chronic neurogenic change; normal motor conduction without block; median sensory amplitudes at the lower limit, sural normal: no current electrodiagnostic evidence of motor neuron disease.
action_criteria.label: EMG and nerve conduction studies of the bulbar, cervical, thoracic and lumbosacral regions to document lower motor neuron involvement and exclude conduction block and neuropathy
action_criteria.rationale: EMG/NCS confirms lower motor neuron involvement beyond the clinically affected muscles and excludes the main treatable mimics: multifocal motor neuropathy with conduction block, demyelinating or sensorimotor neuropathy and myopathy. Gold Coast 2020 accepts EMG evidence of lower motor neuron dysfunction, and Awaji 2008 counts fasciculation potentials as active denervation in muscles with chronic neurogenic change.

action_criteria.label: Brain MRI to exclude structural, vascular, demyelinating, inflammatory or neoplastic causes of the upper motor neuron or bulbar signs
action_criteria.rationale: MRI does not confirm ALS. It excludes brain and brainstem lesions that can cause upper motor neuron or bulbar signs; corticospinal tract signal change, when present, is supportive only.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal cervical and thoracic spine and cord.
action_criteria.label: Spine MRI of the cervical and thoracic cord, and of the lumbosacral spine when lower limb signs need it, to exclude compressive myelopathy, radiculopathy and other cord lesions
action_criteria.rationale: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy with radiculopathy is the commonest structural mimic of combined upper and lower motor neuron signs in the limbs. Spine MRI excludes it, but incidental spondylosis does not explain bulbar signs or denervation in other regions and must not delay the ALS work-up.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TSH 0.1 mIU/L, free T4 2.1 ng/dL and TSI 180% on levothyroxine after radioiodine: thyrotoxicosis; CK normal (148 U/L); blood count, renal and liver function, B12, folate, ESR and CRP normal.
action_criteria.label: Blood tests for treatable mimics: full blood count, renal and liver function, electrolytes and calcium, CK, thyroid function, vitamin B12 and folate, ESR and CRP; plus free T4
action_criteria.rationale: These tests exclude metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory mimics of motor neuron disease; phenotype-specific tests are added only when the case raises that mimic: here thyroid hormone excess on levothyroxine needs free T4 as well as TSH.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 89% predicted and SNIP 78 cmH2O, within normal limits.
action_criteria.label: Baseline respiratory function (FVC and SNIP) as an objective baseline while ALS is not established
action_criteria.rationale: Respiratory function neither supports nor excludes ALS. In a symptomatic carrier without respiratory symptoms or bulbar signs it only provides an objective baseline for follow-up, so it is optional.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansion; no pathogenic variant in SOD1, TARDBP, FUS or TBK1. Carrier status is a genetic risk, not a diagnosis of ALS.
action_criteria.label: ALS gene panel (C9orf72 repeat expansion; SOD1, TARDBP, FUS and TBK1) after pre-test genetic counselling, once the clinical and electrodiagnostic assessment is complete
action_criteria.rationale: Genetic testing does not make the diagnosis. Her father's death from ALS at 58 makes a monogenic cause in the family likely; testing after pre-test counselling defines her genetic risk and that of her relatives, and in a person who does not have ALS it is predictive testing that needs full counselling about its implications.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose ALS or start riluzole on the basis of C9orf72 carrier status and fasciculations.
Do not attribute the weakness to anxiety before the thyroid excess is corrected and she is reassessed.
required_recommendations: Treat the thyrotoxicosis: reduce the levothyroxine dose with endocrinology input (TSH 0.1 mIU/L, free T4 2.1 ng/dL after radioiodine; TSI remains positive, so ask endocrinology to consider residual Graves activity) and recheck TSH and free T4 in 6 to 8 weeks.
Explain that ALS is not established: there are no upper motor neuron signs and EMG shows only simple fasciculations without denervation; reassess strength and fasciculations once she is euthyroid.

Provide post-test genetic counselling about the C9orf72 expansion (ALS and frontotemporal dementia risk); offer counselling to adult first-degree relatives, and defer predictive testing of her teenage children until they can decide for themselves.

Record an objective neurological baseline (MRC grades in named muscles, reflexes, ALSFRS-R) and review in clinic, repeating EMG only if objective weakness, wasting or upper motor neuron signs develop.
Continue support for anxiety and depression, acknowledging her fear of ALS.

avoided_actions.rationale: ALS is a motor-neuron disease without cortical electrical signature; EEG has no diagnostic role and adds cost without benefit.
ECG is unrelated to motor neuron disease and not part of the standard ALS workup absent specific cardiac symptoms or pre-medication QTc checks.
Echocardiography is unrelated to ALS diagnosis; no indication absent comorbid cardiac disease.
Cardiac monitoring has no role in ALS diagnostic workup.
MRI is the standard structural study for ALS workup; head CT adds no diagnostic value and exposes the patient to ionizing radiation.
Amyloid PET has no role in ALS diagnosis (motor-neuron rather than amyloid pathology) and carries a high cost.
DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic integrity; it has no role in ALS, which spares the dopaminergic system.
FDG-PET has no established diagnostic role in ALS and adds substantial cost.

accepted: Thyrotoxicosis from levothyroxine over-replacement in a C9orf72 repeat-expansion carrier, ALS criteria not met

differential.key_features: supports: pathogenic C9orf72 expansion, father with ALS, fasciculations and right hand weakness; against: no upper motor neuron signs, normal CK, EMG with simple fasciculations only and no denervation or chronic neurogenic change

supports: fasciculations for over a year, simple fasciculation morphology, marked health anxiety, possible submaximal effort; against: does not explain the biochemical thyrotoxicosis, which must be corrected first

differential.diagnosis: Persistent or recurrent Graves hyperthyroidism after radioiodine
differential.key_features: supports: TSI still raised (180%) with suppressed TSH and raised free T4; against: she became hypothyroid after radioiodine and takes a full replacement dose of levothyroxine (150 mcg daily), so excess replacement is the simpler explanation; endocrinology review distinguishes the two

differential.diagnosis: Median neuropathy at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome)
differential.key_features: supports: right thenar weakness with possible thenar atrophy, hand paresthesias, median sensory amplitudes at the lower limit; against: paresthesias are in hands and feet and not confirmed on examination
against: normal motor conduction velocities and no conduction block

key_clinical_evidence: Thyrotoxicosis (TSH 0.1 mIU/L, free T4 2.1 ng/dL on levothyroxine after radioiodine, TSI still positive) is a reversible cause of weakness, fatigue, fasciculations, anxiety and poor sleep; it is corrected and the patient reassessed before motor neuron disease is considered.

Simple fasciculation potentials without fibrillations, positive sharp waves or chronic neurogenic change do not meet EMG criteria for lower motor neuron involvement; Awaji 2008 counts fasciculations only in muscles with chronic neurogenic change.

A pathogenic C9orf72 expansion is a genetic risk, not a diagnosis: Gold Coast 2020 needs progressive motor impairment with upper and lower motor neuron dysfunction, which she does not have (no upper motor neuron signs, normal CK, EMG without denervation).
C9orf72 penetrance is age-dependent and incomplete, and the expansion also carries a frontotemporal dementia risk, so counselling for her and her relatives matters.
Predictive genetic testing of minors is normally deferred until they can decide for themselves.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anxiety can amplify symptom perception, but the current medical explanation for weakness and fasciculations is thyrotoxicosis; ALS is not confirmed (no UMN signs, no EMG denervation).
red_herrings.data_point: Anxiety and hypervigilance about her father's ALS
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent to attribute paresthesias and twitching to anxiety or somatic hyperawareness

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Carrier status is a genetic risk, not a diagnosis; Gold Coast criteria are not met.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent to label symptomatic ALS from carrier status

sequence_constraints.reason: Genetic testing follows the clinical and electrodiagnostic assessment and pre-test counselling; it does not make the diagnosis.

patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. V is a 49-year-old nurse and single mother presenting with 8-month history of muscle weakness, twitching, and paresthesias. She is extremely anxious because her father died of ALS at age 58 and she has been fearful of developing the disease. She has noticed widespread muscle twitching for over a year, and over the past 8 months has developed what she describes as progressive weakness, primarily in her right hand and bilateral lower extremities.

She works as a hospital nurse and notes difficulty drawing blood and starting IVs with her right hand. Her colleagues have noted she appears weaker than usual. She also reports numbness and tingling in her hands and feet, which fluctuates. She has had fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and weight changes.

Her primary care physician referred her for neurological evaluation.

neurological_exam.additional: Widespread visible fasciculations. Examination limited by marked anxiety and possible submaximal effort.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue: appears minimally asymmetric but no definite atrophy. No clear fasciculations on brief exam. Speech normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Right hand intrinsic muscles 4/5. Mild right thenar suggestion of atrophy vs contralateral. Otherwise upper and lower extremities near full strength with submaximal effort noted. Widespread visible fasciculations bilateral arms and legs.
neurological_exam.reflexes: All deep tendon reflexes 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor. No Hoffman.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reports paresthesias bilateral hands and feet — not confirmed on examination.
